80.t: His 52nd Street group at the Three Deuces and the Apollo Mother's Day hit
80.s: He had led groups before: a six-piece at the Three Deuces with Benny Waters and Una Mae Carlisle, expanded to twelve pieces for the Apollo, where Mr. Schiffman gave him a gift for a hat.
80.ch: Postwar years, accident and lean times
80.q: No, I had different groups in and out, in and out before that, because I had a group here at 52nd Street. Una Mae Carlisle was playing piano for me, and augmented the band to twelve pieces, went in the Apollo Theater on Mother's Day, and we -- we did so much business, business had been falling off…

80.t: Frank Carey's Brooklyn group with Coleman Hawkins and Rex Stewart
80.s: He first worked with Red Richards on club dates in Brooklyn in bassist Frank Carey's group, which also used Hawkins and Rex Stewart.
80.q: Well now, let me see. I knew Red before I started working with him, but I'm trying to -- (unintelligible) few things here and there, around town, you know. Wasn't nothing too terrific, just a club date here and there, around town. And we were working in Brooklyn, yes. We worked in Brooklyn with the…

220.t: David Wong and Roy Haynes at Birdland's anniversary
220.s: Prompted by Jimmy Heath's remarks on David Wong, Wess recalls Roy Haynes's group at Birdland's 60th anniversary.
220.q: He comes into play with us. I have a lot of good bass players come in. They’re all good musicians that come in. They can all play.

135.t: Monte Kay's Downbeat club and the Symphony Sid All-Stars
135.s: Heath describes the club on 54th Street, Earl May playing left-handed, and the Symphony Sid All-Stars with Miles, Kenny Clarke and J.J. Johnson.
135.q: Right, he and Irving Levy opened the club on 54th Street near 8th Avenue, between 8th and Broadway. And that’s where Billy Taylor’s Trio was playing at, and it’s the first time I saw Earl May standing on the wrong side of the bass playing [chuckles]. He and Charlie Smith were left-handed players,…

104.t: The long Metropole bandstand, dashing to Birdland and sitting in with Duke
104.s: She loved hearing Woody Herman's band strung across the Metropole's narrow stage, then going to Birdland to hear Phineas Newborn, Bud and Duke, who always invited her to sit in.
104.q: . . . across the length of the bandstand. The Woody Herman band would play in there. It would be ridiculous, because at one end would be the drums and piano, and at the far end would be the brass section. I don’t know how they ever got together. They’d all look in the mirror. There was a mirror on…

114.t: Learning on 52nd Street as legends came in
114.s: He stayed 2.5 to 3 years and saw Hawkins, Byas, Lester Young, Webster and Eckstine come to hear them.
114.q: Just to be there, you know, see all the cats and. And, listen, like we'd be playing and we're on 52nd St., right? So we'd be playing and I'd look up and people that I've admired for years, they'd be coming in. I'd look up and -- and in come Coleman Hawkins [phonetic sp.]. I'd look up, Don Byas…

406.t: Sorting out the dates of his work with Coleman Hawkins
406.s: Checking the Encyclopedia of Jazz, he says he played in Hawkins's group at Kelly's Stables between 1938 and 1941, before the Byas two-tenor band.
406.q: I played with Coleman Hawkins -- well, I played with Coleman Hawkins -- we had a band at the Kelly's Stables. And I'm trying to figure when it was. It was somewhere in that area between the time that I was working -- at the time that I came back to New York in '38 and '41 when I took out Ella's…

65.t: Among the first to play Birdland
65.s: Machito's orchestra was among the first Latin band at Birdland, played twenty times for Morris Levy, in late 1949 around the Afro-Cuban Suite.
65.ch: Mambo, the Palladium and Cubop City
65.q: ... so when we were recording - when Bob City or the Birdland was opened, we was involved in Afro-Cuban thing and Morris Levy know us. We know Morris Levy since he was a kid, when he was seventeen or eighteen years old; so they happened to be the owner of the Birdland, so as soon that they opened…

87.t: Raymond Scott's band and Young's own bands on 52nd Street
87.s: He played in Scott's studio band and led a band at the Yacht Club with John Malachi and Tommy Potter, another with Dexter Gordon, after Chicago's Capital Lounge.
87.ch: Earl Hines, Chicago and later gigs
87.q: I don't know. I'd have to go back and find that year when it was. But I had a little band at the Yacht Club on 52nd Street, and my piano player was John Malachi. My bass player was Tommy Potter. I got them out of Washington. And they went with Billy Eckstine later on, the

18.s: They played Kelly's Stable, Three Deuces and Onyx Club with a six-piece band including Billy Taylor and Edmond Hall.
18.q: No, we just played here in New York on 52nd Street. We played Kelly's Stable, we played the Three Deuces, and we played the Onyx Club, all on the same street.

86.t: Opening at Birdland, Roulette and playing opposite Basie
86.s: They discuss Forrest's background; Edison recalls memorable nights at Morris Levy's Birdland.
86.q: Yeah, went to Andy Kirk. And -- but, oh, it was fantastic opening there at Birdland. And then I was signed with Roulette and all the Roulette artists were in Birdland all the time, anyway.
